newsitem.title: USA: Harken plans to spend $30 mln in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Harken plans to spend $30 mln in Colombia.

text.p: Harken Energy Corp said it plans to spend over $30 million in Colombia this year to drill four exploration wells, continue the development of the Rio Negro field, and conduct seismic activities on other identified prospects and acreage.
According to Ecopetrol, the state oil company, Harken has the third largest exploratory acreage position in Colombia behind Amoco Corp and British Petroleum Co Plc.
Harken said it holds roughly one million acres under four association contracts -- three in the Middle Magdalena Basin and one contract in the Llanos Basin.

Pointing out these prospects have varying potentials and are high risk frontier exploration projects, Harken said "a successful discovery at any one of the prospects could have a significant impact on the value of the company."

"Our current estimate of exploration and development drilling costs for Colombia exceeds $30 million in 1997," Chairman Mikel D. Faulkner said. "As in the past, we contemplate funding this budget through cash on hand, cash flow from the company's operations and the involvement of strategic partners."
Harken said it plans to drill one exploratory well on each of the four tracts this year, noting it started the first -- the Estero #1 -- early last month in the Alcarvan contract.
The company said it continues to seek a remedy to the formation damage caused by completion of the Rio Negro discovery well, the Tocaz 2.
Harken said it plans to begin drilling the next well on this prospect -- the Torcaz 3 -- within the next few weeks to be followed by at least two more wells during 1997.
It said the first well exceeded the average well expectations in a geologist's pre-drilling report in terms of formation thickness, porosity, and oil saturation.
The company said an updated reserve report reaffirms that potential recoverable reserves at the level projected before drilling -- could exceed 200 million barrels.

Noting the "very early in the exploration stage" of its Colombian holdings, Harken said calculated reserves on two of the contract areas -- Bolivar and Bocachico -- are already substantial. No reserve calculations have been made for the Cambulos or the Alcaravan blocks. The Alcaravan block is where the Estero 1 is being drilled.
